heading: China Golden Week 2026: Travel Guide for Foreign Visitors
description: Travel to China during October 1–7, 2026? Plan trains, hotels, attractions, crowds and a flexible first-trip route around the National Day holiday.
quickAnswer: China's 2026 National Day holiday runs from October 1 to 7, according to the State Council's holiday notice. Expect popular train departures, major attractions and well-located hotels to require more planning than on an ordinary week. Book the parts that can sell out, keep one flexible block per day, use the exact railway station on your ticket and check each attraction's current entry rules. If your dates are flexible, a visit after the holiday can be easier to pace; if they are fixed, keep your route to fewer cities.

contentSections.title: What are the 2026 holiday dates?

rows: A separate three-day travel period just before October
Seven days of concentrated domestic travel
These are working days in the official schedule, not extra holiday days

items: The State Council schedule establishes holiday dates; it does not guarantee that every attraction opens every day.
Check your destination's own notices before assuming a museum, cableway, park or ticket office follows its usual weekly schedule.
Tourism demand varies by route and weather. Avoid treating a generic crowd ranking as a promise for your exact destination.

contentSections.title: Book the bottlenecks first
items: Confirm your passport-specific entry requirements with an official authority before buying a non-refundable international route.
Choose arrival and departure cities and secure your accommodation before filling in day trips. Verify late check-in and foreign-passport procedures directly with the property.
Check train sales and exact station names on the official 12306 service. Use the document details required for your ticket and make a backup if the desired departure is unavailable.
Check major sights individually for reservation windows, accepted identity documents and timed entry. A third-party travel post cannot confirm an October 2026 slot.
Save your hotel address in Chinese, set up mobile data and payment methods, and keep an offline route for each travel day.

contentSections.title: Build a route that survives crowds

rows: Two or three bases with longer stays
Three or four bases with a rest block
Stacking major ticketed sites on consecutive transfer days

items: Keep the highest-priority ticketed attraction on its own day or pair it with only a nearby flexible walk.
A first-time Beijing, Xi'an and Shanghai route remains possible when the trains and admission windows line up, but do not assume every connection is available.
If the main goal is one nature destination, stay longer there rather than attaching two more distant cities to the same holiday week.

contentSections.title: On a train or airport travel day
items: Use the exact station printed on your ticket: Beijing, Beijing South and Beijing West are separate, as are Shanghai and Shanghai Hongqiao.
Allow extra time for large terminals, passport checks, security and finding the correct platform or pickup zone.
Do not schedule a non-refundable attraction immediately after a long flight or a tightly timed intercity transfer.
Save the train number, Chinese station name and hotel address offline. Check the live 12306 or airline status before leaving the hotel.
Keep a backup meal and local transport option when an attraction queue or rail delay changes your day.

contentSections.title: At attractions and in neighbourhoods
items: Arrive for your confirmed time slot, not just for the venue's general opening hour. Use the same passport or document used for the booking.
Start popular outdoor sites early when entry rules permit, then move to a slower museum, café or local walk rather than chasing several peak-hour queues.
Check weather warnings and last cableway or shuttle departures for mountain destinations. Low visibility can erase the reason for a crowded viewpoint visit.
Use official ticket channels and verify whether a shuttle, cable car, boat or exhibition needs a separate product.
Respect local residents and protected areas; crowd avoidance is not a reason to enter closed paths or residential courtyards.

contentSections.title: If you have not booked yet
items: First check whether your exact trains, hotels and must-see tickets are still bookable. Do not build a perfect route around availability that has already disappeared.
Consider fewer cities, a less central hotel with a good Metro connection, or a later travel week if your dates are flexible.
Avoid unverified claims of guaranteed tickets or priority access. Compare the actual product, cancellation terms and operator before paying.
Keep the Free Trip Starter request specific: dates, entry city, departure city, number of travellers, confirmed bookings and the sights you will not miss.

faqs: When is China Golden Week in 2026?
The official National Day holiday is October 1–7, 2026. Mid-Autumn Festival is a separate September 25–27 holiday.
Should foreign visitors avoid China during Golden Week?
It depends on date flexibility and tolerance for crowds. A fixed-date trip can work with earlier bookings, fewer city changes and flexible daily blocks.
Are all Chinese attractions open during Golden Week?
No blanket rule applies. Check each venue's official holiday notice, reservation channel and timed-entry policy.
Can I buy train tickets at the station instead?
Availability on a popular departure cannot be assumed. Check your date and station on official 12306 and arrange a backup when the train matters to your itinerary.
Is the week after October 7 automatically quiet?
Demand varies by city and date. It may be easier to plan after the official holiday, but confirm prices, availability and local events for your exact dates.
Can ChinaEase Buddy plan around confirmed bookings?
Yes. Provide dates, train stations, hotels, attraction reservations and pace so the route respects what is already fixed.
